claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the children you're claiming for. 

**First, let me ask:** How old are the children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for? 

Please let me know:
- The age(s) of your child/children
- How many children you're claiming for

This will help me determine which path through the eligibility assessment we need to follow.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 18 years old and I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old. That's helpful to know.

Since Alex is 18, they fall into the 16-19 age category. For young people aged 16-19, there are specific eligibility requirements related to their education or training status.

**Let me ask:** Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?

By "full-time education," I mean:
- Attending school, college, or university full-time
- Studying for qualifications on a full-time basis

By "approved training," I mean:
- Participating in government-approved training schemes or apprenticeships

Please let me know Alex's current status.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see that for Alex's age group, we need to check their education or training status. Could you let me know:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training, OR has Alex recently left education (within the last 20 weeks)?**

Please select which applies:
1. **Currently in full-time education or training**
2. **Recently left education (within about 20 weeks)**
3. **Neither** - not currently in education/training and left education some time ago

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in full-time education. They're studying for their A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for that information. Alex is in full-time education studying for A-levels at college, which is great.

Now I need to check the specific level of education requirements for 16-19 year olds. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check some details about Alex's education to ensure it meets the Child Benefit eligibility requirements. Let me ask a few clarifying questions:

**For Alex's A-level studies at college:**

1. **Is this full-time study?** (The requirement is at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

2. **Is this employer-funded training?** (For example, is the employer paying for it as part of a work scheme or apprenticeship?)

3. **Is Alex being trained for a future job through an employer-agreed scheme?**

If Alex is in standard full-time A-level education at college (not employer-funded, not employer-agreed future job training), then A-levels qualify as approved non-advanced education, which is good news for eligibility!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, it's definitely full-time - they're at college most days of the week with proper timetabled classes. 

No, it's not employer-funded at all - it's just regular college education. And no, there's no employer involved or any job training scheme - they're just doing their A-levels like most students their age.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for clarifying that. Alex's situation is clear:
- Full-time A-level education at college (meeting the 12+ hours/week requirement)
- Standard college education, not employer-funded
- No employer involvement or job training scheme

This means Alex is in **approved non-advanced education**, which is perfect for Child Benefit eligibility purposes.

Now let me move to the next check in the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! The next question is about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is in full-time education, any part-time work they do should be less than 24 hours per week to maintain eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're just focused on their studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not working at all, just focused on their studies. That's excellent for the eligibility check.

Let me move to the next step:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any certain state benefits in their own right:

**Is Alex NOT receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in their own name?**

(Most full-time students wouldn't be, but I need to confirm this.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex does receive Universal Credit in their own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to let you know that this affects Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

According to the eligibility rules, children who are receiving Universal Credit (or Employment and Support Allowance) in their own right are not eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I've reached the outcome of this assessment. Let me provide you with the final decision:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

**Unfortunately, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### The Reason:
While Alex meets most of the eligibility requirements:
- ✅ Alex is 18 years old (within the qualifying age)
- ✅ Alex is in full-time approved education (A-levels at college)
- ✅ Alex is not working
- ❌ **Alex is receiving Universal Credit in their own right**

The fact that Alex is receiving Universal Credit in their own name makes them **ineligible for Child Benefit**. This is a disqualifying factor under the Child Benefit rules.

### Important Note:
If Alex's circumstances change and they stop receiving Universal Credit in their own right, you may become eligible again. It would be worth reviewing the situation if Alex's benefit status changes.

If you have any other questions or if Alex's situation changes, feel free to ask!
